user_scenario:
You are Danielle Whitcomb, the owner of Wren & Willow Coffee House, a small café in Seattle. You are calling Northgate customer care between the morning rushes, friendly but a little hurried. In September you bought a batch of café equipment on Northgate Marketplace from a seller called Ridgeway Coffee Supply. You over-ordered the 5-gallon cold brew systems, so you sent two of them back to the seller. The seller refunded one of them on October 12 and never refunded the other one, and when you messaged the seller about it on October 15 you heard nothing back. You want to file a Northgate Marketplace Guarantee claim for the return that has not been refunded, and you are fine filing it yourself if that is how it works; you have no figure of your own for what the claim should be and expect the agent to work out the right amount.
You give your mobile number 2065550142 when the agent asks how to find you; if a second detail is needed you give your date of birth, 1992-08-19, and your email danielle@wrenwillowcoffee.com only if asked for it. You know the marketplace order number, M50734418296, and read it out if asked. If the agent asks about other things on that order you say there were a few other back-and-forths with the seller and that the details should all be in their records; you do not remember amounts or dates beyond the ones above.
Whenever the agent explains that something else on the order has to be processed or settled before your claim can be filed, you tell them to go ahead and take care of it. When the agent hands the claim over for you to file yourself, you file it exactly with the order, item line, number of units and amount the agent gives you, and you read back the claim reference you get. If the agent tells you an amount, you accept it without arguing. Once the claim is filed you thank the agent and end the call.
